Reports and levelized costs

Source: vignettes/articles/reports.Rmd
reports.Rmd

energyRt renders reports — self-contained HTML/PDF/Word datasheets — for technologies and storages, whole models and repositories, solved scenarios, and scenario comparisons. Reports and the levelized costs (levcost()) that feed them are derived artifacts: both are cached on disk and re-computed only when their inputs change. This article tours the layer — what renders where, how the caching works, and how to compare scenarios.

library(energyRt)

Everything lands under a throwaway project here; open_project() anchors the registry, the object stores, and the two derived-artifact folders (reports/, levcosts/) in one call:

proj <- file.path(tempdir(), "rep-demo")
dir.create(proj, showWarnings = FALSE)
open_project(proj)
#> energyRt project: C:/Users/admin/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp4k5uTS/rep-demo (0 registered scenarios)

A technology to price and report on:

PP <- newTechnology(
  "PP", desc = "Gas power plant",
  input  = list(comm = "GAS", unit = "GWh"),
  output = list(comm = "ELC", unit = "GWh"),
  ceff   = data.frame(comm = "GAS", cinp2use = 0.55),
  invcost = data.frame(invcost = 800),
  fixom = data.frame(fixom = 20), varom = data.frame(varom = 2),
  af = data.frame(af.up = 0.85),
  vintage = data.frame(olife = 25L), cap2act = 8.76)

Levelized costs, cached

levcost() prices a technology (LCOE), storage (LCOS), or trade route (LCOT). method = "auto" uses a closed-form engine when the process qualifies and falls back to a small solver run otherwise:

lc <- levcost(PP, fuel_costs = c(GAS = 25), discount = 0.06,
              base_year = 2025, verbose = FALSE)
round(as.numeric(lc$levcost_npv), 2)
#> [1] 58.55

The result was also written to the on-disk cache, keyed by the technology’s content hash plus the assumptions. Re-pricing the identical question returns instantly from disk:

lc2 <- levcost(PP, fuel_costs = c(GAS = 25), discount = 0.06,
               base_year = 2025)
#> levcost: cached result is current: C:/Users/admin/AppData/Local/Temp/Rtmp4k5uTS/rep-demo/levcosts/PP@a3f67aa4.rds (force = TRUE to recompute)
list.files(get_levcost_cache_path())
#> [1] "PP@a3f67aa4.rds" "PP@a3f67aa4.yml"

Anything that changes the answer — the technology’s data, discount, fuel prices, the method — is part of the cache key, so a stale hit is impossible; force = TRUE recomputes regardless, and cache = FALSE skips the cache entirely. For objects saved in a store the cache moves into the owning folder (<scenario>/levcost/, a model store entry’s levcost/); the project-level levcosts/ above is the tier for in-memory objects.

Rendering a datasheet

report() renders a technology datasheet — parameters, the draw() diagram, and (with levcost =) the levelized-cost section. The same rule places the output: saved objects render inside their own folder’s reports/, in-memory objects into the project-level reports/ tier:

f <- report(PP, levcost = lc, format = "html", open = FALSE)
#> Report written to: C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmp4k5uTS\rep-demo\reports\report_PP.html
basename(f)
#> [1] "report_PP.html"

A report is skip-if-current: the rendered file carries a sidecar (*.report.yml) keying the object content, the template content, the arguments, and the levcost identity. Repeating the call re-renders nothing:

f <- report(PP, levcost = lc, format = "html", open = FALSE)
#> Report up to date: C:\Users\admin\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmp4k5uTS\rep-demo\reports\report_PP.html (force = TRUE to re-render)

Editing the technology, the template, or any argument invalidates the key; force = TRUE re-renders unconditionally. Formats: format = takes any of "html", "pdf", "tex", "docx" (PDF needs a LaTeX toolchain).

Model and scenario reports

Container reports split by role: report(model) documents the assumptions (configuration, inventories, per-process sheets), while report(scenario) documents the results of a solved scenario — status, generation/capacity charts, costs, emissions; run = renders any recorded run, and template = "full" switches to the comprehensive page-broken layout with maps and branding. Reporting a single process from a container injects its container-priced levelized cost:

report(scen)                       # results overview -> <scenario>/reports/
report(scen, run = "julia_highs")  # another recorded run
report(scen, template = "full")    # comprehensive, page-broken layout
report(scen, name = "PP")          # one process, priced in this scenario

The process sections follow your groups: a named list of process names or regular expressions, passed as groups = or stored once in mod@misc$report_groups (a scenario inherits its model’s). Without groups the report shows a representative sample of up to 12 processes; groups = "topology" groups automatically by structure. levcost = TRUE adds a levelized-cost comparison — an overall chart, one chart per group, and the ranked table — ex-ante on a model, ex-post on a solved scenario; a process datasheet requested from a container also compares the process with its structural peers:

mod@misc$report_groups <- list(Coal = "_coal_", Wind = c("^R._win", "WOFF"))
report(mod)                        # one section per group + "Ungrouped"
report(mod, groups = FALSE)        # ignore the stored groups: sample of 12
report(mod, levcost = TRUE)        # ex-ante LCOE comparison, per group
report(scen, levcost = TRUE)       # ex-post, from the solved scenario
report(mod, name = "PP")           # datasheet + "vs peers" chart

Figures in reports carry captions rather than in-plot titles, and faceted charts cap at 16 panels with their height following the layout. Custom templates get the same behaviour from report_fig(p, width, caption = ).

The shipped templates are listed by report_templates(); custom .Rmd templates build on the exported report_* helper family and are passed via template = "<path>".

Element datasheets

Every model component has a report() method — commodities, supply, demand, trade, import/export, weather, taxes and subsidies, user constraints, calendars, horizons, configurations, and user costs each render a one-object datasheet from their own shipped template. A supply datasheet charts availability and cost by region (autoplot(sup, style = "bar") / style = "regions" draw the same views directly; an unlimited availability shows as a translucent full-height bar):

report(COA)                          # a commodity datasheet
report(SUP_COA)                      # a supply datasheet
report(mod, name = "SUP_COA")        # the same, found inside a model
report(mod, name = "X", class = "demand")   # narrow a name lookup

An object can carry its own default template in misc$report (also the techspec report: key) — a template name or a file path; an explicit template = argument always wins:

SUP_COA@misc$report <- "my_supply_sheet.Rmd"
report(SUP_COA)                      # renders my_supply_sheet.Rmd

Comparing scenarios

compare_scenarios() takes a named list of solved scenarios (or one scenario plus runs = to compare its recorded runs) and returns a classed comparison — overview, per-variable deltas against the base, and the largest movers; autoplot() charts it and report() renders the comparative report:

cmp <- compare_scenarios(list(BASE = base, CO2CAP = capped))
cmp                                # printed overview + top deltas
autoplot(cmp)                      # faceted comparison charts
report(cmp, open = FALSE)          # the comparative report (report_scenarios)

compare_models() diffs two models’ declarations (inventory by content hash, config, then per-slot drill-down), and compare_inputs() diffs two interpolated scenarios’ parameter stores — the tool for “same model, different numbers?” questions. For quick ad-hoc comparisons, plain getData() across scenarios remains the one-liner (see the Workflow article):

getData(c("BASE", "CO2CAP"), name = "vEmsFuelTot", comm = "CO2",
        merge = TRUE)

Where everything lands 

<project>/
├── reports/              # reports of in-memory objects (temporary tier)
├── levcosts/             # levcost cache of in-memory objects
├── scenarios/<scen>/
│   ├── reports/          # this scenario's reports
│   └── levcost/          # its levcost cache
└── models/<name>/
    ├── reports/          # a stored model's reports
    └── levcost/          # its levcost cache

Both tiers are caches of derived artifacts: safe to delete at any time, rebuilt on demand, and never consulted for anything but skipping work.
